pr_title: Add support for Minecraft Server Bedrock Edition
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Add support for Minecraft Server Bedrock Edition (MCPE: Pocket Edition, MCEE: Education Edition).
- Add new config entry data `TYPE` with default fallback to Java Edition in case of old config entries
- Simplify coordinator by introduction of `MinecraftServer` within `api.py`, which centrally handles both Bedrock and Java Edition servers (used by coordinator, config flow and entry migration)
- Improve device info to easily distinguish between Java and Bedrock Edition
- Add new sensors of Bedrock Edition (edition, game mode and map name) 
- Catch timeout error

Waiting for documentation PR [#29000](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/29000) to get merged before I can add a documentation update for this PR. Until then keeping this in draft state.

**Update**: The mentioned PR is now merged. A documentation PR for this core PR is now created (refer to description).

Just out of curiosity, can't you make JavaServer and BedrockServer a subclass of a MinecraftServer object. This way you can still put the server specifics in that class, but have one way to talk to it, that would avoid a lot of double code in here

> Just out of curiosity, can't you make JavaServer and BedrockServer a subclass of a MinecraftServer object. This way you can still put the server specifics in that class, but have one way to talk to it, that would avoid a lot of double code in here

Probably possible, yes. But I think it would make only sense if I can reuse this new class in the coordinator as well as in the config flow. I'll think about it.
Like, it would save a lot of `isinstance(JavaServer, server)` stuff and it would streamline the way you request any data. the only thing you still need would be to make the bedrock server info async

> Like, it would save a lot of `isinstance(JavaServer, server)` stuff and it would streamline the way you request any data. the only thing you still need would be to make the bedrock server info async

I made following changes locally and it works:
- New module: `api.py` containing new class `MinecraftServer(server_type: MinecraftServerType, address: str)`, which provides functions for checking the connection (for config flow) and for getting data (for coordinator). During init the adress is being checked automatically.
- Move dataclass `MinecraftServerData` and enumeration `MinecraftServerType` to `api.py`.
- Use new class `MinecraftServer` in `coordinator.py`, which significantly reduces complexity.
- Use new class `MinecraftServer` in `config_flow.py`, which makes it slightly better than before.

@joostlek Does this sound OK to you? If so I would push it after some polishing...

I like the direction this is going, I just checked the mcstatus lib and I have something to think about.

Both `JavaServer` and `BedrockServer` are a child class of MCServer. The difference in methods is that BedrockServer looks up sync instead of async.

What about this:
1. we create a `helpers.py` where we have a function `async def lookup(hass: HomeAssistant, server: MCServer)`. In this helper we do a `isinstance(JavaServer, server)` and call the async func, or else throw it in the executor. (You could maybe create another helper that uses this function that gets host and port and checks which of the two it is). 
2. Depending on the amount of checks you still have left for Java/bedrock you could also encapsulate that in a helper.

I am now just writing down what I am thinking, so don't see this as a requirement, just food for thought. At least we are on the track to more abstraction which leads to cleaner code.

> I like the direction this is going, I just checked the mcstatus lib and I have something to think about.

In this helper we do a `isinstance(JavaServer, server)` and call the async func, or else throw it in the executor. (You could maybe create another helper that uses this function that gets host and port and checks which of the two it is).
> 2. Depending on the amount of checks you still have left for Java/bedrock you could also encapsulate that in a helper.
> 
> I am now just writing down what I am thinking, so don't see this as a requirement, just food for thought. At least we are on the track to more abstraction which leads to cleaner code.

Thanks for your input! I think my proposal is similiar to your thoughts. And since you like the direction I'll just push my proposal, since it's ready. Some lines of code says more than 1000 words of comments :smile: 

In my proposal I use the `lookup` function within the initialization itself, therefore we don't have to think about async in that case.

I think I commented somewhere earlier that I'm detecting and storing the server type in the config entry data to speed up the initialization and data update. Otherwise I would have to check for Bedrock Edition first and if it fails retry with Java Edition. In worst case this is 9 seconds of waiting time (3 retries, 3s timeout each).

And some information regarding `mcstatus`:
Yes, both `JavaServer` and `BedrockServer` are subclasses of `MCServer`. `BedrockServer` uses the base implementation for `lookup`, correct. For the `JavaServer` an own implementation is used, which also checks and resolves SRV records. `async_status` is used to check the connection to the server and to get updated data, but this function is specific for each server type.

> While checking if all requested changes of @joostlek were addressed, I found that the lookup is not done in the executor.

I was thinking that it's not required, because the lookup is done in the contsructor, which is not async anyway. But you're right, I'm using the constructor in an async function/context. I'll try to put them in the executor.

Oh for some reason after a restart (I wanted to make debug logs) it actually succeeded into migrating it.

Should this be catched as well as the ValueError you now do?

Hmm at first glance it looks like the lookup function of mcstatus doesn't catch `dns.resolver.LifetimeTimeout` properly. But I have to check this in detail. Thanks 👍 

In your case the migration failed initially, but HA gets to know about it, because the migration will return False in that case, so it can be retried later.
This is something I would like `mcstatus` to handle, since the exception is from their dependency `dnspython`. I created an issue over there, let's see...
Oh that's a good one as well

The maintainers of mcstatus rejected to handle the exception on their own, so we probably have to catch it within the integration.

But to understand the timeout better: What address did you use? Host only? Host with port? Or SRV record? You also said that the server was offline during migration. In case of host or SRV record: Do you know if the DNS server was also offline?

And is this worth fixing in 2023.10? Or should I just fix it in the current open PR, which if everything goes well will probably be in 2023.11?

review_comments:
I like the idea! I don't really like the idea of splitting up the retrieving logic into the coordinator and this api class.

What if in the `__init__.py` you (use a helper to) try to lookup the server type, after which we pass the MCServer to the coordinator. With as added benefit, if the server can't be looked up, we can say that the config entry is not ready.

Then you can put the rest of the mapping logic in helpers to not make the coordinator one big pile of code.
I think it would be nice if the coordinator shouldn't have to know what kind of server he is talking with and put those specifics away in functions, making the coordinator clean

Good point, thanks :+1: 

I create now the API instance (`MinecraftServer`) in `__init__.py` and pass it to the coordinator. If a problem with the config entry is detected, `ConfigEntryError` is now raised (before, `HomeAssistantError` was raised instead in the coordinator).

I also reached now a state, where I cannot further simplify the coordinator. It's now as simple as it can get :smile: 

I still stick to the server type stored in the config entry data and not to detect the server type in `__init__.py` due to the possibly long waiting times I mentioned before.

BTW: `ConfigEntryNotReady` is already handled by `coordinator.async_config_entry_first_refresh`, called in `async_setup_entry.`
Make this a set instead of a list.
We should patch the library client not our code.
Even if I plan to add tests of the api module, where I would then patch the library?
Yeah. We should avoid writing the tests to be dependent on integration details. Avoiding that allows refactoring the integration without changing any tests.
I plan to add more tests in general soon, will take care of this in one of those future PRs.
Please make sure your config flow tests ends either in a config entry created or abort to show it can recover from a failure

In each test I already check for `FORM` or `CREATE_ENTRY`. Do you mean the order of the asserts? Should the check for flow result be always the last assert in the test function? Or do you mean something else?
you only check for form, but we want to see that after an error message, the flow is able to succeed

Sorry, I'm a bit lost here. I checked a few other integrations and didn't see much of a difference. The config flow of Minecraft Server either is successful (`CREATE_ENTRY`) or it cannot connect. In that case the same `FORM` is shown only with a difference, that the error message is shown additionally. In that form the user can correct the user input and retry.

It's something that we like new tests to have, to avoid code that could stick around and put the config flow in some kind of lock. So the trick is to finish the FORM, so it will become either a CREATE_ENTRY or an ABORT

My problem is, that I don't abort my config flow, therefore (if I understood correctly) I can never reach the ABORT state. Let me try to make this more clear with screenshots.

This is the initial form. I entered an invalid input and after confirming we come to the second screenshot.
![Bildschirmfoto vom 2023-09-27 10-19-02](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/1382097/15b886c8-a35c-4103-8894-1a6ab44a399c)

After the config flow detected a connection error, the same form is shown with additionally the error message.
![Bildschirmfoto vom 2023-09-27 10-19-40](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/1382097/646d04a1-2385-427a-9cbd-727de62a1cd1)

So the config flow doesn't abort the flow, even if a connection error is detected.

Understood, but then we would like the tests to first reach the state where we show the user an error, and then retry again with valid info, making it succeed. This is to make sure the config flow doesn't end up in an unsolvable state.
This is something I can add, no problem. Thanks :+1:
hah, explaining isn't my strongest point, but we got there in the end :)
Done, added a new test case for config flow recovery (successful connection after a failed one).
